copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 avoids the recycled 'machines aren't rising up' joke and exclamation-headline shape that sink Candidate 1, and its blurb, 'OVER EUROPE, FIGHTERS SHEPHERD THE FRIGHTENED AIRLINERS', wears the grand 1940s newsreel form far better than Candidate 3's flat 'morning flights', while the summary

doom.driver: Hoax or bomb threats? What we know about flight disruptions across Europe. Security inspections reveal no explosives as fighter jets escort planes amid Europe's major wave of bomb threats.
doom.blurb: OVER EUROPE, FIGHTERS SHEPHERD THE FRIGHTENED AIRLINERS
doom.summary: Nobody has found a single explosive, yet Europe is scrambling fighter jets to babysit passenger planes, which is a very expensive way to deliver a prank call. Meanwhile Moscow and Tehran are swapping rocket launchers like trading cards, and the AI boom is learning that a midterm landslide is louder than any keynote. NASA's Swift telescope also chose today to plunge into the sea off Indonesia, a fitting metaphor for nobody in particular.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: No new frontier leaps today, just MCP explainers and an AI trade bleeding on the stock ticker.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Voters, bankers and Amsterdam protesters are all leaning on the data center buildout at once, but this is friction rather than freefall.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia arming Iran with rocket launchers, plus a cooperation treaty in the works, deepens an axis that is already in the fight.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: The machines kept their schemes to themselves today.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A continent-wide wave of bomb threats has fighter escorts in the sky, and hoax or not, someone is testing Europe's nerves.

doom.dalle_prompt:
Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A wide, ground-level view across a remote parking stand at Venice Marco Polo airport at night, in the long hours after a bomb-threat diversion has been declared a hoax. The flat apron runs to the edge of the lagoon. Beyond a low fence, wooden bricole mooring posts stand in mist that glows blood orange, and a faint Venetian skyline of bell towers sits on the horizon. The sky is a bruised violet, striped with the thin, fading contrails of two fighter jets that have long since left. Every surface is lit from below by volcanic orange light. It comes from low ground-level floodlight bars and from the wet tarmac, which mirrors them in molten streaks, so the whole scene is bright and clearly readable. The shadows are plum and maroon.

At center stands a white Wizz Air A321 with a magenta tail, its belly and engines glowing orange from beneath. Its forward cargo hold is open, and the passengers' suitcases are lined up in neat rows on the tarmac beside it, waiting to be reloaded. A tracked bomb-disposal robot with its articulated arm folded sits parked in the foreground, rimmed in orange light. Next to it stands a technician in a bulky blast suit with the helmet off, whole and facing the plane, looking tired and calm. A police handler in a dark uniform and hi-vis vest sits beside a spaniel, which has its tongue out. In the middle distance a Polizia officer, whole and walking, winds up a long coil of striped cordon tape. A red fire engine and a bomb-disposal van stand idle with their light bars off, and the fire engine's red paint glows orange.

The mood is menacing and uneasy. The danger has passed, but the tarmac still looks hostile and wrong. Violet and blood-orange tones dominate, and there are almost no cool colors.

minor: The "Wizz" logo on the fuselage is stylized pixel lettering that reads roughly as "WIZ". It is small and plausible, not obvious gibberish.
The aircraft's rear stairs, cargo loader and wing area are a bit muddled where they overlap near the engine, and the tail and wing edge look slightly fused. It still reads as a plane.
The dog's body blends into the handler's legs and the orange ground, but it still reads as a spaniel with its tongue out.
The cordon-tape officer in the background is a dark silhouette, and the tape coil is hard to make out.
The row of silhouetted figures or posts along the horizon is ambiguous. They are distant and fit the bricole posts and crowd the prompt described.
The bomb-disposal robot's arm and claw are a bit tangled, but the robot reads clearly.
Strong orange and red saturation flattens some details, but nothing is too dark to read.

dawn.driver: Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky.
dawn.summary: A spacecraft launched in 1977 has just become the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth, so a message from home now takes a full day to reach Voyager 1. Overhead this month, fireballs, a close pairing of Mars and Jupiter and a supermoon give everyone a free show without leaving the backyard. Down here, a small trial found that four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in people carrying a high-risk Alzheimer's gene.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Low-dose rapamycin boosted brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged APOE4 carriers within a month, with women showing the strongest gains.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Nearly 5,800 volunteers helped show that heart calcium scans can guide statin use as safely as traditional risk scores while prescribing to far fewer people.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Diyarbakir's Amedspor has climbed from Turkey's third tier to a top-of-the-table match in the Super Lig, carrying a proud fan base along with it.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: After two years of testing, a reviewer has found kitchen composters worth recommending, making it easier to turn food scraps into soil.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth, a distance no spacecraft has ever reached, nearly half a century after launch.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 wears the understatement directive well with 'SOMEWHAT FAR' and steers clearest of the 11-04 card's 'one full light-day from home… still sending word back' phrasing, which Candidate 3 nearly copies and Candidate 1 partly echoes; it also adds a fresh, specific line about the free backyard

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. GROUND-LEVEL VIEW from deep in the grass of an open hillside meadow, looking steeply upward at a grassy crest against a huge, clear, pale-blue afternoon sky. Late-afternoon daylight is balanced and steady, with clear golden-yellow sun and fresh spring-green grass, and a confident, warm glow over everything. Giant foreground blades of bright green grass frame the bottom corners. A towering old maple in golden-yellow autumn leaves rises on the right, its branches spreading across the upper frame. On the crest stand a mother and her young daughter, both fully visible and seen from below, with their backs partly turned and their faces tipped toward the eastern horizon in patient, bright-eyed anticipation. The mother wears a mustard-yellow knit sweater and holds a folded plaid wool blanket and a steel thermos. The girl wears a green puffy vest and holds a big chunky flashlight pointed up at the sky, switched off, as if saving it for later. Two folding camp chairs lean against the maple trunk, and a woven picnic basket sits in the grass beside it. The sky above them is empty and wide, so the coming night is implied only by their posture and their prepared gear. Crisp pixel clusters, dithered golden light on the grass and leaves, and long soft shadows stretching down the hill.

minor: The girl's flashlight is held out to the side and looks a bit like binoculars or a camera, not a flashlight pointed up.
The mother's arm holding the plaid blanket is hard to read, since the blanket hangs behind her hip with no clear hand or arm gripping it.
The green camp chair is partly hidden behind the red one, so the two blend together a little against the trunk.
The giant foreground grass blades are soft and blurry next to the crisp pixel clusters elsewhere, but they frame the scene as intended.
